Step 13 (lines 1958-1976) then expires ALL APPROVED signals whose combo_key is not found in any PENDING signal from the last 5 minutes. Since the preserved signal is the ONLY signal for this token+direction (no PENDING row exists), approved_ids stays empty, the else branch fires, and the APPROVED signal gets expired. The decider (line 2229) calls get_approved_signals() which queries decision=APPROVED AND executed=0 - finds nothing.
bugs.fix: signal_compactor.py Step 13 (lines 1936-1980): Added AND combo_key NOT IN (top10_combos) to BOTH the if and else branches of the APPROVED signal expiry logic. This prevents expiring APPROVED signals whose combo_key is in the current hotset_final, regardless of whether approved_ids is empty or not. The if branch was the one actually firing (PENDING signals exist), not the else branch.

bugs.title: PRESERVE-APPROVED-UPSERT creates zombie loop — stale signals survive indefinitely via created_at=CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
bugs.symptom: Preserved hotset entries get APPROVED rows with created_at=CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, refreshing their age. The compactor's 10-minute query picks them up again, creating an infinite cycle: DB→hotset→preserve→UPSERT→DB. Signals like ema300-dip can maintain perpetual hotset slots, accumulating survival_rounds (observed up to 108) while the two staleness checks in decider_run.py are dead code because get_approved_signals() does not return created_at or entry_origin_ts.
bugs.root_cause: Three interacting bugs: (1) PRESERVE-APPROVED-UPSERT (signal_compactor.py:2267-2285) writes APPROVED rows with CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, refreshing the signal's age to 'just now'. (2) get_approved_signals() (signal_schema.py:2645-2683) SQL SELECT does not include created_at or entry_origin_ts, so decider_run.py:2728 (V2 staleness check) and decider_run.py:3045 (accel staleness check) are dead code — sig.get('created_at') always returns None. (3) entry_origin_ts resets to time.time() (signal_compactor.py:1813) when a preserved entry drops and a new PENDING signal fires, restarting the staleness clock.
bugs.fix: PRESERVE-APPROVED-UPSERT has 30-min age guard ([PRESERVE-APPROVED-AGE-BLOCK]) and INSERT uses original entry_origin_ts as created_at instead of CURRENT_TIMESTAMP. get_approved_signals() SELECT includes created_at (FIX 2026-09-04).
bugs.verified_by: daily-orchestrator code inspection + get_approved_signals SQL
bugs.orchestrator_note: Previously OPEN (OPEN). Re-verified fixed 2026-10-01 by daily-orchestrator.

bugs.title: brain.py trade add dies (argparse RC=2) on negative scientific-notation signal values — trades silently fail
bugs.symptom: 64 RC=2 "usage:" trade failures in 4 days (2026-10-03..08); BLUR LONG retried & failed every minute 14:25-14:31 UTC on 2026-10-08. Log showed only the argparse usage block, never the error line.
bugs.root_cause: decider_run.py built brain.py argv as ["--signal-macd-hist", str(v)]. Python renders tiny negative floats in scientific notation (e.g. -4.29e-06). argparse's negative-number matcher (r'^-\d+$|^−?\d*\.\d+$') does not match "-4.29e-06", so argparse treated it as an OPTION → "error: argument --signal-macd-hist: expected one argument" → RC=2 → trade never opened. Any token whose signal had a negative MACD hist/value in sci-notation (common for low-price coins) was un-tradeable.
bugs.fix: All brain.py argv options in decider_run.py now use the "--opt=value" equals form (helper _barg) which argparse accepts for any value incl. negative scientific notation.
bugs.verified_by: Reproduced parse failure with extracted parser (space rc=2 / equals OK); LIVE CONFIRMED 2026-10-08 14:43:42 UTC — BLUR LONG trade #15989 opened after failing every minute 14:25-14:31 pre-fix.

bugs.title: pump-exit momentum exit reads the WRONG end of the candle window — counts oldest candles, not newest
bugs.symptom: Momentum exit (pump_exit_momentum) fires on stale momentum and misses current dumps. With newest-2 candles dumping hard the old code returned False (LONG held a falling knife); with newest-2 recovering it returned True (cut a winner). Affects every pump_chain+ trade — all 3 currently-open trades (GRASS/FOGO/BLUR) map to pump_exit and RR_EXIT_ENABLED=True.
bugs.root_cause: _vel_closes fetched ORDER BY ts DESC (index 0=newest) but the loop ran range(1,len) — newest interval first, oldest last. The consecutive counter RESETS on a non-qualifying candle, so the final surviving run reflects the OLDEST intervals, not the newest. Direction semantics (LONG exits on vel < -0.5, SHORT on vel > +0.5) were correct; only the window end was inverted.
bugs.fix: Iterate the range in reverse (oldest interval → newest) so the newest interval is evaluated last and the surviving counter run is the most recent candles. Both LONG and SHORT branches.
bugs.verified_by: Reproduced the exact loop logic standalone: newest-2-dumping → old=False/fixed=True (want True); newest-2-recovering → old=True/fixed=False (want False); SHORT mirrors both pass. py_compile OK. Path confirmed live via SIGNAL_EXIT_CONFIG (pump_chain+ → pump_exit) + 3 open pump-chain trades.

bugs.title: watchdog autopilot wrote brain DB BEFORE HL attempt with no rollback — stop divergence
bugs.symptom: Every failed HL stop-move left brain DB stop_loss updated while exchange stop unchanged; position_manager then pushed its own view, silently overriding the watchdog.
bugs.root_cause: execute_safe_actions called adjust_stop_loss(trade_id,...) before replace_sl; on HL failure the DB write was never reverted.
bugs.fix: Reordered: HL replace_sl FIRST, DB adjust_stop_loss only on hl_result success.

bugs.title: decider_run sl-zone sizing ATR inverts TR pairing — DESC list not reversed (unfixed twin of position_manager fix)
bugs.symptom: SL-zone size adjustment used a slightly-wrong ATR: query ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 20 but the TR loop did not reverse, so rows[i] (OLDER candle H/L) was paired with rows[i-1][3] (NEWER close) — inverting the previous-close pairing. Impact minor (ATR still captures range magnitude) but inconsistent with the identical calc in position_manager.py ~2714 which DOES .reverse() first.
bugs.root_cause: Missing _atr_rows_zone.reverse() before the TR loop over a DESC-fetched candle list. Found by BUG-039 pattern sweep (subagent) as a sideways finding — it is NOT the BUG-039 consecutive-count pattern (no reset counter), just an inverted TR pairing.
bugs.fix: Added _atr_rows_zone.reverse() before the TR loop, matching position_manager.py.
bugs.verified_by: py_compile OK; cross-checked against position_manager.py ~2714 twin which reverses first. BUG-039 sweep subagent confirmed this was the only unfixed DESC/ASC inconsistency of its kind in scripts/.

bugs.title: 1m candle pipeline degraded — aggregator dead (MIN_BARS=3 vs exactly 1 tick/window by design) + seed rotation too slow for 178 tokens
bugs.symptom: hermes-1m-candle.service prints [1m] filled=0 closed windows, dev=0 tokens on every run (0 writes since 2026-10-05 21:34). candles_1m: only ~30/178 tokens fresh <5min; the rest rotation-stale 5-31min (median ~11min at 21:47 UTC; user measured median ~22min/max 31min during a slow-cadence period). All alt-token 1m RSI/BB/EMA consumers read up to 31min-stale closes.
bugs.root_cause: (1) Commit e9a299ca (2026-10-05 21:32) raised MIN_BARS_FOR_CLOSED 1->3 and MIN_BARS_FOR_DEVELOPING 1->2 in _aggregate_1m.py:29-30, premised on 'price_history ticks are ~155s apart'. Actual: ticks are written EXACTLY ONCE per 60s window BY DESIGN (signal_schema.py:4487 minute_ts=(now//60)*60 + INSERT OR IGNORE at :4489). Verified over all 13.3M rows back to 2026-08-25: 100% of 1m windows have exactly 1 tick; ZERO windows ever have >=2. So bar_count>=3 (_aggregate_1m.py:127) and bar_count>=2 (:192) can never pass — aggregator is 100% dead code. This shutdown was noticed but accepted in brain/verdicts/bug-hunter-candle-pipeline-fix.md (2026-10-05 22:20), trading the aggregator for INSERT-OR-IGNORE safety with '~36min staleness worst case' explicitly accepted. (2) With the aggregator dead, candles_1m freshness for all 178 universe tokens depends solely on price_collector._seed_universe_candles rotation: 178 tokens / TOKENS_PER_RUN=10 = 17.8 runs x measured effective run cadence 36-142s (timer says 30s but Type=oneshot cadence collapses to run duration; avg 67s over 32min, ~92s in recent half) = 18-42min full rotation. The skip-if-fresh logic (price_collector.py:237-241) NEVER fires (every run logs 'Seeded 10/10') because rotation period >> 300s threshold. BTC exempt (always fetched, :264-269). (3) Latent landmines that make a naive MIN_BARS revert dangerous: (a) last_closed_dict walk-back (_aggregate_1m.py:82-89) uses the OLDEST stuck is_closed=0 dev row as fill boundary when dev_ts < lc — 94/185 tokens currently get a boundary 24h-45d old (most at 08-26 02:22) -> a MIN_BARS=1 revert attempts ~5.5M IGNORE no-op fills/run (verified by read-only simulation; matches the 4.9M fill-storms recorded in the 10-05 verdict) instead of the ~800 real live-edge windows; (b) closed path INSERT OR IGNORE can never upgrade an existing is_closed=0 dev row (K-tokens: 230,827 stuck rows, is_closed=1 count=0 all-time) — a dev-close UPDATE is required; (c) tokens with no is_closed=1 row ever are skipped entirely by lines 105-106 (chicken-and-egg).
bugs.fix: PROPOSED (not yet implemented — CEO decision pending): PRIMARY: split the seeder into a fast 1m-only refresh loop (1 API call/token, e.g. 60-90 tokens/run => all 178 fresh <2min with REAL OHLC+volume) and the existing slow multi-TF backfill loop (15m/1h/4h every ~18min, 5m ~8min). Restores sub-5min 1m freshness for ALL 178 tokens with real volume, keeps flat candles out entirely, removes dependence on the aggregator. INTERIM MINIMAL (if aggregator must be reactivated): _aggregate_1m.py: MIN_BARS_FOR_CLOSED 3->1, MIN_BARS_FOR_DEVELOPING 2->1, KEEP INSERT OR IGNORE, PLUS (i) fix boundary: use lc when dev_ts <= lc (last_closed_dict[token] = max(walkback, lc)) to prevent 5.5M-fill storms; (ii) close dev rows via UPDATE ... SET is_closed=1, open=?,high=?,low=?,close=? WHERE token=? AND ts=? AND is_closed=0 before INSERT OR IGNORE; (iii) accept that live-edge fills are flat (O=H=L=C) volume=0 for 0-18min until the next seed REPLACEs them with real OHLC — close-based RSI/BB stays accurate, but volume gates read 0 at the edge (documented tradeoff). REJECTED: revert-to-1 alone without (i)/(ii) = fill-storm + DB lock contention; 'reject high==low or volume==0' quality gate = aggregator writes NOTHING again (verified: 100% of would-be fills are high==low by construction, 1 tick/window); MIN_BARS=2 = still dead (0 windows with >=2 ticks since 2026-09-01); raising price_history tick density = breaks the 1-bar=60s signal contract.
